newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields edge higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields edge higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Swedish debt yields were slightly higher around midday on Monday in line with somewhat weaker foreign markets, untouched by a downward revision of the state borrowing requirement for 1997.
"It's extremely quiet," a dealer said. "Foreign markets have weakened somewhat and this has affected long Swedish yields."
The crown ignored the weaker dollar and strengthened to 4.5255 against the mark from 4.5330 late on Friday.
Six-month T-bill rates rose one basis point to 4.21 percent and the ten-year bond yield was up three basis points at 7.06.

"In the case of Sweden, the EMU issue is still looming and hampering the market," an analyst said, referring to that the minority Social Democratic government is expected to voice its opinion about EMU membership in May.
The crown strengthening could be a correction as the crown, which usually tracks the dollar, recently has softened when the U.S. unit has firmed, dealers said.
The National Debt Office lowered its forecast for 1997 government borrowing requirement by 10 billion crowns to 10-20 billion from 20-30 billion early in the session.
